ideas.title: Restock Alerts for Square Online

notes.stateful: The shop keeps a saved list of shoppers waiting per item and size, plus a demand history the owner checks before reordering.
notes.connected: Connects to the shop's own Square account by OAuth (catalog and inventory) and runs a script on the shop's Square Online site.
notes.unattended: Square's inventory webhook and a 15-minute scheduled check detect a restock and email the waiting shoppers with no action by the owner.
notes.shared: Shoppers sign up and receive the alert; the owner gets the demand report from the same data.

buildPlan.title: One item, one alert
buildPlan.delivers: The owner signs in, connects Square and installs the script through the Snippets API; the script maps a sold-out product page to its Square catalog item (address id, then SEO permalink or name as fallback); a shopper leaves an email, and a 'check now' button emails them once stock is back.
buildPlan.acceptance: On a test Square Online site the page-to-item mapping is proven for 10 products; a sign-up on a sold-out item followed by a stock count above zero produces exactly one email with a working product link; the app is deployed at its hintwise.org address.

buildPlan.title: Sizes, colours and page changes
buildPlan.delivers: The panel asks which variation the shopper wants, recognises both zero counts and manually marked sold-out items at the site's selling location, and follows product-to-product navigation without a page reload.
buildPlan.acceptance: For an item with three sizes, only subscribers to the restocked size are emailed; the panel shows and hides correctly across 10 in-site navigations; no code depends on the page's class names.

buildPlan.title: Automatic restock detection
buildPlan.delivers: Signed inventory.count.updated and catalog.version.updated receivers (the latter followed by SearchCatalogObjects from a stored begin_time, to catch items marked sold out or back by hand), a 15-minute scheduled reconciliation through BatchRetrieveInventoryCounts, de-duplication and an option to alert only as many shoppers as units restocked.
buildPlan.acceptance: A replayed webhook sends no duplicate email; un-marking a manually sold-out item triggers its alerts; with webhooks switched off, the scheduled job still catches a seeded restock within 15 minutes.

buildPlan.title: Consent and unsubscribe
buildPlan.delivers: A consent record per sign-up (wording, time, page), one-click unsubscribe, the shop's name and postal address in every alert, optional double opt-in, and automatic deletion after the alert or after 180 days.
buildPlan.acceptance: The unsubscribe link works without signing in and stops all further alerts; the consent export lists wording and time for every sign-up; expired rows are deleted by the nightly job.

buildPlan.title: Demand report
buildPlan.delivers: A dashboard of waiting shoppers per item and size, most-wanted sold-out items, sign-ups over time and alerts sent, with CSV export.
buildPlan.acceptance: Counts match the database for a seeded data set of 50 sign-ups across 8 items; the CSV opens cleanly in a spreadsheet.

buildPlan.title: Install fallback and polish
buildPlan.delivers: A Tracking Tools paste-in fallback for owners who cannot use the Snippets install, an owner README with a setup checklist (including showing sold-out items on the site), phone layout, keyboard and screen-reader pass on the shopper panel, walkthrough test.
buildPlan.acceptance: A new owner goes from sign-in to a live panel in under 10 minutes by either route; axe reports no serious issues on the panel or the dashboard; the walkthrough test passes.

ideas.summary: For small shops on Square Online: shoppers who find a sold-out item can ask to be emailed when it returns, the email goes out by itself when stock comes back, and the owner sees which items people are waiting for.

public.summary: Lets shoppers ask to be emailed when a sold-out item in your Square Online store is back, and emails them by itself when you restock.
public.problem: When something sells out in your Square Online store, a shopper who finds it has no way to ask to hear when it returns, so they leave and often don't come back. You answer emails and calls asking when things will be back, and you reorder without knowing which items people are actually waiting for.
public.forWhom: Small shops selling on Square Online whose products sell out and come back: boutiques, plant nurseries, gift, toy and craft shops, and specialty food sellers.
benefits: Shoppers who find a sold-out item leave their email instead of leaving empty-handed
They hear as soon as you restock, without you sending anything
See which sold-out items people are waiting for before you reorder
Fewer 'when will it be back?' emails and calls
Works with the store you already have

ideas.problemStatement: Square Online has no way for a shopper to ask to be told when a sold-out item returns. Sellers have asked since 2019: "The 'Notify me when back in stock' has been a feature request from countless users for many years and it's still being ignored" (2026-09-07); "it's absolutely INSANE that customers have been asking for this feature for years now" (2026-04-15); "We get customers asking via email and phone when out of stock items are likely to be back in stock"; and a plant grower says that on a prior platform the feature "was a significant driver of sales for us".
ideas.description: The shop owner signs in, connects Square by OAuth and installs one small script on their Square Online site, through Square's Snippets API (no approval is needed outside the App Marketplace) or, as a fallback, pasted into Tracking Tools. On a product page the script maps the page address to a Square catalog item: the 24-character id in the address matches the catalog-id format on one store checked, but Square staff said in 2022 that item ids are not available to snippets and Square Online keeps its own site product ids, so the first milestone proves this mapping, with the item's SEO permalink or name as the fallback. The backend then checks whether that item or size is sold out at the site's selling location, and if so the script shows a small 'email me when it's back' panel that does not depend on the page's layout. Square's inventory.count.updated webhook, plus catalog.version.updated for items marked sold out by hand and a 15-minute scheduled check, detects when stock returns and sends each waiting shopper one email with a link back to the product, the shop's details and an unsubscribe link. The owner sees how many shoppers wait for each item and size, and can export the list.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners of small retail shops selling on Square Online (Free, Plus or Premium) whose items sell out and come back: boutiques, plant nurseries, gift, toy and craft shops, specialty food sellers.
ideas.buyer: The shop owner, on the business card, from the same small online-store budget that pays for Square Online.
ideas.whyNow: Square shipped a stream of inventory features through 2026 (scheduled stock resets in July, preorders for sold-out variations with a reset time on 2026-09-24, Volumes 1 to 17 of its product updates through 2026-11-19) but still no shopper sign-up for sold-out items, while sellers kept asking (2026-04-15, 2026-07-24, 2026-07-28, 2026-09-07, 2026-11-04). Square's Snippets API now lets an app place a script on Square Online sites, and Klaviyo's Square Online integration (updated 2026-10-28) still offers no back-in-stock flow for it. Holiday-season sell-outs make the gap most visible now.
ideas.founderFit: Pisan ships small web apps alone in days, and this one is a contained integration on the HintWise platform as it stands: one storefront script, Square OAuth, a webhook receiver, a scheduled job and transactional email. It needs no domain knowledge he lacks.

ideas.techStack: Static owner dashboard; a small framework-free storefront script served from the static host; backend-hub on Render for Square OAuth, the signed inventory.count.updated and catalog.version.updated webhooks (the catalog event names no object, so the app calls SearchCatalogObjects with a stored begin_time) and the public sign-up endpoint; shared Supabase for owner accounts, encrypted Square tokens, waiting lists and the consent log; HintWise transactional email for alerts; a scheduled job for reconciliation (BatchRetrieveInventoryCounts), token refresh and deletions. Square APIs: OAuth, Catalog (ITEMS_READ), Inventory (INVENTORY_READ), Sites and Snippets (ONLINE_STORE_SITE_READ, ONLINE_STORE_SNIPPETS_WRITE) as the main install, with Tracking Tools as the fallback.

pricing.model: Per-shop monthly subscription with a free tier
pricing.pricePoint: Free up to 25 alert emails a month; $9/month up to 1,000; $19/month up to 5,000
pricing.rationale: Below the $19/month Starter plan Shopify merchants pay for the same job (https://apps.shopify.com/back-in-stock), because many Square Online shops run on the free plan and are price-sensitive; a free tier lets small shops see sign-ups before paying.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate only. Assumes 40 paying shops by month 12 (from a free tier several times larger) at an average of $12/month: 40 x $12 = $480 MRR, about $5,800 a year. Email costs stay small at these volumes. The figure rests on unmeasured conversion from the free tier.
ideas.distribution: First 10: (1) the Square Seller Community, where the buyers are named in the 'Notify me when back in stock' threads (topics 849060 and 630340); the community's etiquette page could not be read (empty page), so its promotion rule is unconfirmed; a search summary of it says spam includes excessive self-promotion and members should not promote their own products or services unprompted, so reply only where sellers ask for a workaround. A seller-developer's post about their own Square tool (topic 852023, 2026-11-02) drew a supportive reply on 2026-11-19, which suggests seller-built tools are tolerated when useful. (2) Direct install with no marketplace listing: the owner connects Square by OAuth and the app installs its script through the Snippets API; the fallback is one line pasted into Tracking Tools (Free, Plus and Premium, https://squareup.com/help/us/en/article/6957), though Square says tracking code 'isn't intended to be visible'. (3) Later, the Square App Marketplace: listing needs approved partner status, and snippet integrations need Square's explicit approval after a stringent review (https://developer.squareup.com/docs/snippets-api/overview). Square-seller Facebook groups and Reddit were not checked.

validationTest.method: Build milestone 1 and run it free for 3 weeks with 5 Square Online shops that sell out often, recruited from the two Square community feature-request threads (replying only where sellers ask for a workaround) with a one-page explainer; count sign-ups per sold-out item and whether owners switch it on for their whole catalog.
validationTest.successCriteria: 3 of 5 shops keep it installed for 3 weeks, at least 2 collect 20 or more sign-ups, and 2 owners agree to pay $9/month after the trial.
validationTest.cost: 2 build days; $0 beyond the HintWise platform.

ideas.moat: Thin. The value is in Square-specific details (manual sold-out flags as well as counts, per-location stock, sizes and colours, a layout-independent panel that survives Square Online page changes) and in each shop's growing waiting lists and demand history, which make switching mildly costly. Square could ship this natively at any time; that sellers have asked since 2019 without it shipping is the main reason to expect the gap to last a while.
compliance: CAN-SPAM (US): an alert whose primary purpose is to sell the restocked item is likely commercial email, so it needs an accurate sender (the shop), a postal address, a working opt-out honoured within 10 business days, and no deceptive subject; the shop and the sender can both be liable (https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business).
CASL (Canada): express consent from the sign-up form, with the shop identified and an unsubscribe in every alert.

GDPR and UK GDPR, and Australia's Spam Act (Square Online sells in these markets): consent limited to this one alert unless a separate marketing box is ticked, a consent record, deletion after the alert, and a data processing agreement with each shop (the app is a processor).
CCPA/CPRA: likely below thresholds; support deletion requests passed on by the shop.
Accessibility: the shopper panel and dashboard should meet WCAG 2.2 AA (keyboard, screen-reader labels, no focus traps).
Square's Snippets rules: disclose what the script collects, stay out of checkout, and do not call Square APIs from the browser.
No payments, no text messages (avoids TCPA and 10DLC) and no health data.

risks.mitigation: Keep the price low and the build small; lists export at any time; the demand report and variation-level alerts remain useful. Square has listed the request as 'Not currently planned' (2022) and 'Unspecified' (2025) with no 2026 announcement.

risks.risk: Square Online page changes break the panel.
risks.mitigation: Read the item id from the page address, not the layout; show the panel as a fixed overlay rather than inserting it into page elements, per Square's warning about class names; run a daily automated check against a test site.

risks.risk: The product address may not carry the catalog item id: Square staff said in 2022 that ids are not available to snippets, and Square Online keeps separate site product ids.
risks.mitigation: Make the mapping milestone 1's first task: test the address id against the catalog on a test site, and fall back to the item's SEO permalink (CatalogEcomSeoData.permalink) or name.

risks.risk: Shops hide sold-out items, so shoppers never see the page.
risks.mitigation: The setup checklist checks for and explains the 'display out of stock items' setting.

risks.risk: Multi-location shops: the online site sells from one location's stock.
risks.mitigation: The owner picks the site's selling location at setup; alerts follow that location's counts.

risks.risk: Alerts land in spam or draw complaints.
risks.mitigation: Send from a verified domain under the shop's name, offer double opt-in, rate-limit, and remove bounced and unsubscribed addresses at once.

ideas.title: Booking Rules Page for Square Appointments

buildPlan.title: Connect Square, test enforcement, take one booking
buildPlan.delivers: The owner signs in and connects Square; the app first tests whether a buyer-level availability search and booking still work with the location's Square online booking and Square Go turned off, then a hosted page lists one location's services and open times and books a client into Square.

public.summary: A booking page that follows your rules, such as which services run on which days, set start times and returning clients only, while every booking still lands in your Square calendar.
public.problem: You want facials only on weekday evenings, or clients to start at 11, 2 or 5, but your Square booking page offers every service at any time you are working. The fix you are offered is to create pretend staff profiles, and odd start times leave gaps you cannot fill.
public.forWhom: Owners of small salons, spas and nail, lash, skincare and massage studios who take bookings and payments with Square Appointments and want to keep it.
benefits: Each service offered only on the days and times you choose
Clients start at the times you set, so fewer dead gaps
Close booking to new clients without shutting out your regulars
A card on file for your no-show policy
Your calendar, reminders and checkout stay in Square

ideas.problemStatement: Square Appointments ties online availability to staff working hours only, so owners ask to "restrict individual services to specific days of the week", to reserve "evenings and after-school hours" for facials, to offer start times "such as 11 AM, 2 PM, and 5 PM" because other times "create gaps", to "turn off online booking to new clients but leave it available to existing clients". A spa owner told to create extra staff profiles wrote: "I have limited time before I give up on square and migrate my business to another platform."
ideas.description: The owner connects Square and sets rules per service: allowed weekdays and hours, fixed start times, an option to offer only times next to existing bookings, and a returning-clients-only switch. The hosted or embedded page reads open times from Square (cached, because Square's booking rate limit is low), filters them through the rules, takes the client's card on file through Square's own card form when the owner's policy needs it, and books the client into Square Appointments, so Square's calendar, reminders and checkout keep working. Square's API cannot book a service that carries a Square cancellation fee, so no-show protection comes from the saved card, which the owner charges from Square. Square's own booking site, Square Go and Square's reschedule links do not know the rules, so the first milestone tests whether API bookings still work with Square's online booking switched off (which would make the page the only public channel); if not, the product is sold honestly as rules on the page plus a morning email listing any booking made elsewhere that breaks a rule. Returning clients are matched against the owner's Square customer list. Keeping a home address private is left to Square's own free workaround, explained in the setup guide.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners of solo and small (1 to 6 provider) salons, spas, skincare, nail, lash and massage studios that run bookings and payments on Square Appointments, including the free plan, and do not want to leave Square.
ideas.buyer: The owner, on the business card, from the software budget that already pays for Square (Square's own plans run from a free plan to paid tiers).
ideas.whyNow: Square's feature log shows Appointments changes through 2026-08-20 (add-ons, dark mode) and per-service deposits on 2026-05-14, but still no per-service availability or start-time control, while owners opened eight separate threads asking for these between 2026-08-31 and 2026-11-15. Square's API docs say an outside app can make buyer-level bookings for every seller, free plan included; Square staff confirmed in October 2026 that such bookings are accepted at once when the owner accepts all bookings, and in November 2026 that an unlisted app needs no marketplace listing or fee, so a small add-on can book on an owner's behalf today.
ideas.founderFit: The core is a scheduling-rules engine over open time slots with a lock against double booking, which suits a CS professor who ships small web apps alone in days; the rest is a Square OAuth connection and a booking page on the HintWise platform.

compliance: Privacy: client names, emails and phones from a public page; publish a privacy policy, keep minimal fields with row-level security per business, delete data when the owner disconnects Square; GDPR for UK and EU sellers, CCPA/CPRA for California clients where it applies.
Square Developer Terms: least-privilege OAuth scopes, no implied Square endorsement, and a clear 'not affiliated with Square' line.
Accessibility: the client booking page should meet WCAG 2.1 AA (US ADA claims against small businesses' booking flows are common).
Payments: no card data in the MVP; if card-on-file is added later, use Square's hosted card fields so card data stays with Square (PCI DSS SAQ A).
Email: confirmation and address emails are transactional; no marketing email without consent (CAN-SPAM, and UK/EU e-privacy rules).
Health data: salons and spas are not HIPAA covered entities, but massage and skincare intake answers can be health information; the MVP does not collect or store intake answers.
Consumer protection: show the business's own cancellation policy accurately on the page; no texts in the MVP, so TCPA/10DLC does not apply.

ideas.problemStatement: Square Appointments sends messages only before a visit. Owners say "I can't believe a simple post appointment automated communication option still hasn't been added" and want different aftercare per service ("if they go for a Pregnancy Massage I should be able to send different aftercare than if they've had a Hypnotherapy appointment"). Stylists rebook clients on 4- to 10-week cycles by memory: "It's impossible to remember everyone's usual cycle", and they count weeks back through appointment history by hand.
ideas.description: The owner connects Square once. The app reads a year of bookings and customers and works out each client's usual gap between attended visits, ignoring vacation gaps and letting the owner set a preferred interval. A nightly job emails a rebook reminder, with the owner's booking link, to clients who are past their usual interval and have no future booking; no-shows and cancellations are skipped, and a new booking arriving by webhook cancels any queued reminder. This appointment-aware engine is the part neither Square nor Klaviyo's order-based Square flows can do. As a second feature, the owner writes a short aftercare email per service, sent a set time after the booking's end (no checkout or order needed), with an optional Google review link at a delay the owner chooses. A phone-friendly list shows each client's interval and booked status for use at checkout. Unsubscribes, Square's own email opt-out and a results page of who rebooked are built in. It works on Square's free plan because it only reads bookings.
ideas.targetCustomer: Solo and small salons, barbers, lash and brow artists, nail techs, massage therapists and aestheticians on Square Appointments whose clients return on personal cycles of 3 to 12 weeks.

ideas.whyNow: Square's feature releases of 22 October, 5 November and 19 November 2026 (Volumes 15 to 17) add AI tools and receipt links but no message after a visit, while sellers asked for one from January to September 2026. Square's AI assistant can now draft a win-back email for clients who have not booked in 60 days when the owner asks (2026-11-12), which shows the value but leaves it manual. The Bookings API lets an app read every booking without a paid Appointments plan, so the app also reaches solo owners who cannot use Square's paid marketing automations.
ideas.founderFit: Pisan ships small web apps alone in days. The work is one OAuth integration plus a scheduling engine over booking history (interval estimation, suppression rules, webhook-driven cancels), which is algorithmic CS work that fits the HintWise platform's scheduled jobs and transactional email.

Promotion rule: not read; the Community Etiquette Guidelines page returned an empty bot-gate response (HTTP 202), so the Marketer must read it before posting anything. 2) Square App Marketplace: a Square employee wrote on 2026-10-01 that onboarding of new apps is paused (https://developer.squareup.com/forums/t/listing-square-apps-marketplace/28043), so the app is reached by a direct Connect Square link until it reopens. 3) Search pages for 'Square Appointments aftercare email' and 'rebooking reminder for Square'.

validationTest.method: Ship milestone 1 as a free read-only client rhythm report (connect Square, see each client's usual interval and who is overdue with no future booking) on a landing page that offers aftercare and rebook emails as a paid beta; share it only where the Square Community rules allow, and through the search pages.
validationTest.successCriteria: Within 30 days, 20 Square sellers connect and at least 5 start the paid beta at $15/month; record how many ask for texts, which decides whether email-only is enough.
validationTest.cost: About 2 build days and under $100 (domain and test email volume).

ideas.moat: Thin. Templates, overrides and interval history build up in the app, and the interval engine with future-booking suppression and webhook cancels does what Square's fixed timers and Klaviyo's order-based flows cannot, but Square has the building blocks (Squaremates, hosted apps) to add it.
compliance: CAN-SPAM (US): rebook reminders are commercial email: honour opt-outs within 10 business days, include a postal address and an honest subject line; aftercare whose primary purpose is care or safety information about a service the client bought can be transactional, so keep promotions out of aftercare emails (https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business).

Consent outside the US: Square's own Australian help says emails collected for a booking cannot be used for marketing without explicit consent (https://api.squareup.com/help/au/en/article/5660); CASL (Canada), UK PECR and EU GDPR and ePrivacy also restrict marketing email, so rebook reminders go only to clients the owner marks as opted in outside the US. The CRTC's CASL FAQ returned 403 and was not read.

Square's email opt-out flag (CustomerPreferences.email_unsubscribed) is read-only, so the app must honour it and keep its own unsubscribe list (https://developer.squareup.com/reference/square/objects/CustomerPreferences).

Washington My Health My Data Act: service names such as pregnancy massage can be consumer health data (the WA AG treats inferred pregnancy data as protected, small businesses covered since 2024-06-30) (https://atg.wa.gov/protecting-washingtonians-personal-health-data-and-privacy); store only booking dates, service IDs and names, and client email; let owners exclude services; publish a health data privacy policy. The Act binds processors (the app is the salon's processor, so it needs processor contract terms) and is enforced through private actions as well as by the Attorney General.

HIPAA: not expected for salons and massage studios; a medical spa that is a HIPAA covered entity would need a business associate agreement, so the MVP imports no notes or forms and is not offered to covered entities.
TCPA and 10DLC: not triggered while the app sends email only.
Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA for the owner app and plain, readable emails.
Data handling: encrypt Square OAuth tokens and delete a seller's data on disconnect.

risks.risk: Square adds a post-appointment message type or schedules Squaremates win-back emails.
risks.mitigation: Lead with the per-client interval engine and future-booking suppression; month-to-month pricing; watch Square's monthly release notes. Square's Squaremates can now email customers with approval and build hosted custom apps, so the risk is higher than it looks; keep the interval engine and future-booking suppression as the core.

risks.risk: Owners asked for texts (the 2026-08-28 post is titled 'text reminders'), and the platform sends email only.
risks.mitigation: Show each owner's email coverage in milestone 1; the validation test counts text requests before any SMS work.

risks.risk: Many clients book with a phone number and no email.
risks.mitigation: Report coverage up front and add an email-capture tip to the booking confirmation copy.

risks.risk: No App Marketplace listing while onboarding is paused.
risks.mitigation: Direct Connect Square link, search pages, and community answers where allowed; apply when onboarding reopens.

risks.risk: Health-related service data for massage and aesthetics.
risks.mitigation: Minimal data, service exclusions, privacy policy, no notes or forms.

risks.risk: No COMPLETED booking status, so a visit is inferred.
risks.mitigation: Treat ACCEPTED bookings whose end has passed as visits, honour NO_SHOW, and let the owner fix a wrongly sent email's cause in the log.

risks.risk: The Square Community, where the buyers and the evidence threads are, moves to a new platform before the end of 2026, so thread links and the LiQL API may change.
risks.mitigation: Keep the human thread URLs beside the API URLs, and build search pages for the exact questions so reach does not depend on the threads.

scoreRationale.pain: Six sellers on four Square Community pages ask in 2026 for messages after the visit or help rebooking on personal cycles, most recently 2026-08-28 and 2026-09-24: https://community.squareup.com/api/2.0/search?q=SELECT%20subject%2C%20body%2C%20post_time%2C%20author.rank.name%2C%20depth%20FROM%20messages%20WHERE%20topic.id%20%3D%20%27850080%27%20ORDER%20BY%20post_time%20ASC%20LIMIT%2030
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: One paid plan for the job, NiceJob Pro at $135/month for rebooking reminders (https://get.nicejob.com/pricing); no paid jobs; the one seller paying a third party pays for review timing, and the Square Marketing payer's complaint is from 2025.
scoreRationale.reachability: Buyers are in named Square Community threads (topic 770017 has over 28,000 views), but App Marketplace onboarding is paused (https://developer.squareup.com/forums/t/listing-square-apps-marketplace/28043.json) and the Community moves to a new platform before the end of 2026.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Klaviyo's native Square integration already sends per-item post-checkout and timed win-back emails from $0 to $20 a month (https://help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/11117215837211-Getting-started-with-Square-Online), Square Plus has fixed-timer lapsed automations and Squaremates drafts win-backs on request; only the appointment-aware rebook engine is unserved.
scoreRationale.feasibility: Seller-level booking reads work without a paid plan and booking.created and booking.updated webhooks exist (https://developer.squareup.com/docs/bookings-api/what-it-is); ListBookings filters by customer in 31-day windows (https://developer.squareup.com/reference/square/bookings-api/list-bookings); there is no COMPLETED status (https://developer.squareup.com/reference/square/enums/BookingStatus), and email-only falls short of owners who asked for texts.
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Rebook reminders are commercial email under CAN-SPAM (https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business) and need opt-in in several Square markets (https://api.squareup.com/help/au/en/article/5660); massage and aesthetics service names can be consumer health data in Washington (https://atg.wa.gov/protecting-washingtonians-personal-health-data-and-privacy).

review.findings: An adversarial reviewer (stopped by the account's usage limit and resumed four hours later) confirmed six independent sellers asking in 2026 for post-visit messages or rebooking on each client's own cycle, with two posts within 90 days that read as owners but drew no replies, one of them asking specifically for texts. It found the draft missed Klaviyo's native Square integration, which already sends per-item post-checkout and timed win-back emails from $0 to $20 a month, and that Squaremates can now email customers with approval, raising the risk that Square ships this itself. willingnessToPay fell from 4 to 3 (one paid plan, no paid jobs; the only paid workaround is review timing) and competitiveGap from 3 to 2, so the total is 20 and the idea is provisional, re-scoped to lead with the appointment-aware rebook engine for Square Free sellers, with aftercare and an optional delayed review link second.

watchlist.targetCustomer: Salons, studios, clinics and solo service providers in British Columbia, Alberta and Manitoba who take bookings in Square Appointments or Calendly.
watchlist.problemStatement: Appointments saved before the vendor's time-zone update sit an hour off; one salon owner has over 200 to check by hand, and Square support says no patch is coming.

watchlist.title: Local Order Status Desk for Shopify Pickup and Own-Driver Delivery
watchlist.targetCustomer: Small grocers, bakeries and boutiques on Shopify that offer store pickup and deliver with their own drivers.
watchlist.problemStatement: Native local delivery orders cannot be edited, and the shipping-rate workaround loses the local statuses and sends a 'shipped' email for collected orders.
watchlist.missedGate: Not researched; competitiveGap 2 (EasyRoutes free plan and Zapiet already send local status messages; the edit block is in Shopify's platform).

watchlist.title: Payment-Plan Collector for Partly Paid Shopify POS Orders
watchlist.targetCustomer: Bridal boutiques, furniture shops and custom jewellers that take a deposit at the counter on Shopify POS and collect the balance over months.
watchlist.problemStatement: Staff negotiate a schedule at the counter but must chase every instalment by hand; Shopify does not charge the balance on its due date.
watchlist.missedGate: Not researched; pain 3 (one detailed merchant plus agreement), and a new $17/month POS layaway app may be close enough.

watchlist.targetCustomer: Small Shopify food makers and shops selling pickup-only items next to items they ship.

watchlist.missedGate: Not researched; pain 3 (one complaint plus the mandate) and competitiveGap 2 (Printer Pro and a December launch at $9/month).

runNotes.caveats: No idea cleared the gate as gathered without losing points in research or review; one ships validated at exactly 22 (Restock Alerts for Square Online, willingnessToPay 3 at the floor of its band: Shopify spend for the same job, no Square seller seen paying) and two ship provisional to fill the day to 3. Six candidates were researched and four adversarially reviewed: none killed, three rescored down (Booking Rules 22 to 21, Rebook Reminders 22 to 20, Cancellation Waitlist 20 to 18) and one passed (Restock 22). Review stopped once 3 ideas had survived; the waitlist survived review but did not ship because the fill stops at 3. Concentration: all three ideas are Square add-ons, and two serve the same customer (small salons and studios on Square Appointments) with different problems; the Square Seller Community's LiQL API was today's richest complaint vein, and Square says that community moves to a new platform before the end of 2026, so its API evidence URLs may stop resolving. No selected idea is a Weekend MVP: all three are substantial Multi-week builds with a buildPlan, and no Weekend MVP candidate met the floor with a review, so the Weekend MVP constraint is not met. Friday's focus sources: A13 (community.shopify.com) produced six candidates, all at 21 or below because most customer-facing Shopify threads are written by app developers; B11 produced spend-only candidates with no complaints; C8 trade news produced mandates but almost no dated owner complaints. This environment changed on 2026-11-20 (the routine now runs in the FullInternet environment), so scripts/probe_sources.py --write re-measured the catalog first: A1 and B5 went to blocked, C3 to ok-curl. The run was interrupted by the account's 5-hour usage limit from about 10:46 to 14:40 UTC; one review was resumed afterwards and the run finished at about 15:30 UTC.
